establishedBehavior.registration: The real Node installer API creates separate application/build registrations and immutable cached native payloads. The four registered graphics cells use different application identities but the same generation19 native/JavaScript bytes; distinctNativeBuilds=false is retained.
establishedBehavior.selfLoad: Real ReShade AddonPath scanning maps both registered add-ons with both applications offline; initial private participant/slot/window/rank/TCP/frame-worker counts are zero. The supplying application of the first dispatcher stays offline when the other app activates at its existing mapped base.
establishedBehavior.productionInjection: The initiating public SDK creates one owned host before devices, returns the strict four-field first-host result, and activates the exact scanned selected application. Its peer stays dormant; this lane does not claim both apps were offline initially.
establishedBehavior.isolation: Controller assertions cover isolated alpha/bravo delivery and colliding local IDs, interleaved alpha surfaces, individual raising, caption dragging, three cursor shapes, wheel behavior and requested/effective interception OR acknowledgements.
establishedBehavior.interceptionScope: The preload controllers assert requested/effective ACK state; these four registered cells do not separately measure native game-input counter freezing.
establishedBehavior.lifetime: Crashing one application removes its surfaces/input while the survivor keeps its private identity, route and interaction. Restarting the consumed application maps exactly one fresh ordinary engine; unregister changes future snapshots without changing the live target.
establishedBehavior.finalRegisteredState: After all apps exit, each registered case retains three mapped engines, participant slots and frame workers until target exit; TCP/windows/ranks/focus/capture/interception requests are zero. This is not zero native-thread or zero retained-participant state.
establishedBehavior.gen16Compatibility: The retained installed unregistered generation16 SDK joins dynamically while the registered current dispatcher application is offline, then survives that application's crash. It is not claimed to support preload registration. Final mixed cases retain two engines/slots/frame workers with zero active TCP/window/input ownership.
establishedBehavior.configuration: External snapshots and owned staged INIs are intentionally created; the packaged 209-byte template remains sealed. No ReShade DLL/add-on/INI is installed in the copied target directory. This is not a claim that test markers or the copied demo EXE are absent.
establishedBehavior.logs: The audited D3D11 logs contain shutdown warnings for a bounded outbound drain on an already disconnected transport after app exit. They are not described as warning-free.

pairedSmallStackRegression.scope: Actual candidate DLL thread attach/detach under the same inert console API shim. No ReShade runtime, graphics, private transport or input acceptance.
pairedSmallStackRegression.stackReservationLimit: The values are requested stack sizes; Windows rounds reservations. Passing them does not prove actual16KiB/32KiB reservations.

oldX64Disassembly.meaning: The old x64 DLL reserves the large frame before checking notification reason. Both architecture negatives overflow; only this exact x64 frame size is claimed.

pairedSmallStackRegression.correction: Filename classification now runs in a non-inlined process-attach helper using bounded heap storage, keeping the notification entry frame small. The final actual DLLs complete all three worker entry/detach sequences.

failureHistory.causalLimit: The diagnosed generation17 CPU stack overflow does not explain the earlier historical generation9 D3D11 GPU device-hang incident. No complete historical SDK/graphics-harness byte equivalence is claimed for all diagnostic iterations.

limits: No user game was used for this feature, and historical generation16 game results are not generation19 reruns.
Preload/compatibility graphics acceptance is x64 on controlled D3D11/D3D12 demos. The additional D3D9/D3D10 x86 default-path passes do not establish x86 preloading graphics support.
Both registered app identities use the same generation19 bytes; only the separate current19/old16 dynamic-join lanes establish mixed-native-version behavior.
Pre-device D3D12 barriers do not establish generic late-D3D12 queue recovery.
Preloading is opt-in for a new owned host; it does not make an existing host rescan, replace its host, or change a foreign installation's configuration.
Older member-readiness-only injectors can time out on manually configured stock-only dormant hosts. Current feature scope is latest owned hosts; ReadyV1 meaning is not changed into dormant readiness.
Registration/cache import checks, console policy validation, actual DLL notifications and graphics feature cells establish different scopes.

Native modules, participant slots and frame workers intentionally remain resident after consumed sessions. Shared address space is not native fault containment, and500-app/version capacity or flat memory usage is not measured.
The strict disablement/elevation policies are covered by native console/source checks, not by modifying a user-managed stock game installation.
DPI/OSR labels identify the requested attached-surface regression configuration; they do not independently prove that a requested raster/display mismatch was observed.

postAllGuiPublicVerification.scope: Confirmed by the active controller after all GUI cases; read-only public verifyOverlayPackage, no package writes.

ownedCleanup.scope: Final CIM/process and lease cleanup confirmed by the active controller. PC sleep is handled only by the root after all work.
